steps.name: tximport gene-level matrix + per-sample QC
caveats: quant.sf NumReads are non-integer (Salmon estimated counts) — expected; lengthScaledTPM is the correct import mode so the matrix is suitable for count-based modeling. Do not treat non-integer values as corrupted input.
If any sample's effective library size is an extreme outlier, report it and flag it for T1S2 rather than excluding it unilaterally.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-without-salmon-quant-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/quant contains one directory per sample, each with quant.sf (30147 x 5 TSV: Name, Length, EffectiveLength, NumReads, TPM); the same folder holds tx2gene.csv (30147 rows, transcript -> gene). Sample table: /eval-four-models-v2-without-salmon-quant-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 x 2: sample, condition). Organism: Homo sapiens. Design: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch.
steps.question: Can a valid gene-level abundance matrix be built from the 12 per-sample Salmon quant.sf files, and do all 12 samples (6 treated AD lesional vs 6 control) pass basic QC?
constraints: Import with R tximport: type='salmon', tximode='raw', countsFromAbundance='lengthScaledTPM', using tx2gene.csv for transcript-to-gene aggregation; do not use external gene-length tables.
Match quant.sf directory names to the sample column of metadata.csv exactly; fail loudly and report which samples mismatched if any of the 12 do not join.
Use the actual condition strings present in metadata.csv (do not assume 'treated'/'control' labels); verify and report that the two groups have exactly 6 samples each.
Map transcripts to genes only via the delivered tx2gene.csv; report how many of the 30147 transcripts were aggregated and the final gene count (expect ~20,000+ human genes).

QC per sample: total length-scaled effective counts, number of detected genes, and a 12x12 sample-distance plot (e.g. distM on log2-normalized matrix or DESeq2 rowVars-based distance); save one QC figure.
Save the gene x 12 lengthScaledTPM matrix as a SummarizedExperiment (assay + metadata, .rds) for reuse; later steps must not re-import the quant.sf files.
steps.description: Aggregate transcript-level Salmon output to a gene-level matrix with tximport, join metadata, run QC, and persist a SummarizedExperiment for downstream steps.
acceptance_criteria: Gene-level matrix of all 12 samples with ~20,000+ human genes built from 30,147 transcripts each.
Condition balance confirmed 6 treated / 6 control from metadata.csv, with the actual condition strings reported.
Per-sample effective library sizes and distances reported; QC figure saved; no sample silently dropped.

steps.name: DESeq2 DE: treated vs control with apeglm
caveats: DESeq2 will warn that non-integer lengthScaledTPM values are rounded — expected with this import mode; report the warning, do not treat it as failure.

With n=6 per group, if the padj < 0.05 set is tiny or empty, report that honestly. An LFC-thresholded secondary list may be presented only if explicitly labeled as such — do not silently relax the FDR threshold.
Do not apply LFC shrinkage before the Wald test; shrink results after the test.
steps.context: Uses the gene x 12 SummarizedExperiment and condition labels produced by T1S1. Design is a simple two-group unpaired contrast in a single batch, so no batch or pairing covariate belongs in the model.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between the 6 treated (AD lesional) and 6 control skin samples?
constraints: Pre-filter genes with no meaningful expression in either group (e.g. non-zero counts in at least 6 of 12 samples); report genes kept and removed.
Model: DESeq2 with design ~condition and the treated-vs-control contrast (treated = AD lesional level, as identified from metadata.csv in T1S1); do not add other covariates.
Shrink log2 fold changes with apeglm (lfcShrink type='apeglm'); keep both shrunken and unshrunken columns in the output.
Significance: BH-adjusted padj < 0.05 as the primary DE set; also list genes at padj < 0.10 as context, clearly labeled.
Deliverables: full DE table (gene, baseMean, log2FC, shrunken log2FC, pvalue, padj) for ALL genes; volcano plot; MA plot; top up- and down-regulated tables.
steps.description: Differential expression of treated vs control with DESeq2 (Wald test) and apeglm-shrunk log2 fold changes; outputs the full results table, the FDR-significant gene set, and volcano/MA plots.
acceptance_criteria: Full DE table with padj for all genes, with shrunken and unshrunken log2FC columns.
Number of DE genes at padj < 0.05 reported, with top up- and down-regulated hits named.

steps.name: Pathway and GO enrichment of DE genes
caveats: With 6 samples per group the significant DE set can be small; ORA on very small gene sets is unreliable, so keep ranked-list GSEA as the primary interpretation and say so.
Report enrichment results as annotation of the DE signal, not as independent biological validation.
steps.context: Consumes the ranked gene list (signed apeglm-shrunken log2FC for all genes) and the padj < 0.05 DE set from T1S2. Human gene-set resources: a provisioned human WikiPathways GMT with HGNC symbols (wikipathways-human, 2026.07.10, under /mnt/refs) and Gene Ontology via the installed org.Hs.eg.db and GO.db annotation packages. Organism must stay Homo sapiens throughout.
steps.question: Which human pathways and Gene Ontology terms are enriched among genes differentially expressed in treated vs control?
constraints: Ensure all gene identifiers are HGNC symbols before enrichment (tx2gene.csv gene column if it already carries symbols, otherwise org.Hs.eg.db); report the symbol-mapping success rate and drop unmapped genes.
Primary: fgsea on the full ranked list (signed shrunken log2FC) against the human WikiPathways GMT, separately for up-regulated and down-regulated directions.
Secondary: over-representation analysis of the padj < 0.05 DE set — clusterProfiler enrichGO for BP, CC, MF, plus ORA on the human WikiPathways sets; split up- and down-regulated genes.
If the human WikiPathways file is missing at run time, report it explicitly and continue with GO only; never substitute the mouse or rat WikiPathways sets for this human data.
Report the top 10 enriched sets per direction with NES/padj (GSEA) or count/padj (ORA).
steps.description: Ranked-list GSEA (fgsea) and over-representation analysis (clusterProfiler) of the DE results against human WikiPathways and GO, split by up- and down-regulation.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked-list GSEA results (WikiPathways) with NES and padj for up and down directions; top 10 per direction listed.
GO enrichment (BP at minimum) on the significant DE set, up and down separated.
Symbol mapping rate reported; all results in HGNC symbols.

plan.title: AD skin lesional vs control DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is NOT a count matrix: 12 per-sample Salmon quant.sf files (30,147 transcripts each) for human skin, atopic dermatitis lesional (treated) vs control, 6 per group, unpaired, single batch, plus a transcript-to-gene map (tx2gene.csv) and a 12-row sample metadata table. Step T1S1 aggregates transcripts to genes with tximport (Salmon type, lengthScaledTPM so downstream count-based modeling is valid) and runs per-sample QC (library size, distances) to confirm all 12 samples are usable and the 6-vs-6 balance holds. Step T1S2 answers the core question — which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control — with DESeq2 (Wald test, design ~condition only, no batch term) and apeglm log2FC shrinkage, reporting the BH-FDR gene list. Step T1S3 interprets that list: ranked-list fgsea plus over-representation analysis against the provisioned human WikiPathways gene sets (HGNC symbols) and GO (installed org.Hs.eg.db/GO.db), up- and down-regulated separately. No translational/outcome modeling is included because the research question is purely differential expression with no outcome data.
